doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mother's piano and gospel singing at home
summary: His mother played stride piano, the children sang gospel through the vents, and she corrected him as a teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But didn’t you also sing with your mom and your sisters?
Oh yes.
Tell us about that.
That was a thing that my mother was an old-time piano player. Hot dog. That lick.
All right. I’d like to hear that.
I loved that. When she felt like doing it, we were upstairs in the different rooms where we slept. They had those vents in the furnace, but they were in all the rooms, and you could hear downstairs.
Ah, you could hear the music coming through.
Yes.
And that got you excited.
That’s what we would get next to.
Oh, you put your ear next to the vent.
Yeah. She’d be playing, and then we’d start singing.
What kinds of songs?
Gospel.
Gospel songs.
Yeah. We were a family raised in the gospel.
Your mom knew how to play piano, and she had taught herself how to play piano?
I don’t know exactly how she – but I believe that was it. She taught herself. She’d just get on that piano and strut.
She could play stride piano.
Yeah. I [?], knowing it was her or hot dog, that’s my big shot.
Did she early on identify you as a person who had musical talent? Did she early on tell you, “Jimmy, you got a beautiful voice. You can sing.”?
She would hear me sing, and I was more or less – she’d say, “[?], you didn’t sing that song right. No, no.”
So she’d – so she’d – if you missed the note, she would tell you.
Missed a note or didn’t sing a phrase right. No, no.
So Momma was a strict teacher. This is how the song goes.
Yes. She was a teacher for me more than anything else. She never expressed to me that I was a singer and I had to do this or that or the other.
